questions.stem: What is the equation for density?
questions.explanation: Density is calculated using the equation density = mass / volume, or in symbols, rho = m/V.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of density?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of density is kg/m^3 (kilograms per cubic metre). It is also commonly expressed as g/cm^3.

questions.stem: An object has a mass of 500 g and a volume of 250 cm^3. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume = 500 g / 250 cm^3 = 2 g/cm^3.

questions.stem: An object floats in water (density 1.0 g/cm^3). What must be true about the object?

options.text: Its density is less than 1.0 g/cm^3
Its mass must be very small
Its density is greater than 1.0 g/cm^3

questions.explanation: An object floats when its density is less than that of the liquid. Since water has a density of 1.0 g/cm^3, the floating object must have a lower density.

questions.stem: How can you measure the volume of an irregular solid?

options.text: Use a displacement method with water in a measuring cylinder
Weigh it in air and in water
Measure its length, width, and height

questions.explanation: The volume of an irregular solid is found by submerging it in water and measuring the volume of water displaced (the rise in water level).

questions.stem: If 1 g/cm^3 = 1000 kg/m^3, what is the density of aluminium (2.7 g/cm^3) in kg/m^3?
questions.explanation: To convert g/cm^3 to kg/m^3, multiply by 1000. So 2.7 g/cm^3 = 2.7 x 1000 = 2700 kg/m^3.

questions.stem: Two blocks are made of the same material. Block A has twice the volume of Block B. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Block A has twice the density of Block B
Block A has half the density of Block B
Both blocks have the same density
Block A has four times the density of Block B

questions.explanation: Density is a property of the material, not the size of the sample. Both blocks are made of the same material, so they have the same density regardless of volume.
